name: modelbrain-mcp

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Liveness check that never touches the store. Use `diagnostics` for anything more.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Find the memories nearest a query, best first. Required: `query`. Check this before saying you don't know something about the user; it is not consulted automatically. Hits carry `key`, `text`, `relevance`, `created_at`, `source_date`, `partition`, `source`, `tags`. Read dates from `source_date` (when the content happened), not `created_at` (when it was indexed): resolve relative dates against it and prefer the later one when two hits disagree on a fact. For a "connector" hit cite `source_uri`, not `key`. Unbound connections search every active partition; `partition_scope` narrows ("all" adds archived). Use `scope: "user"` for what the user told you. Pending and superseded memories are hidden by default. Filters: `tags`, `object_type`, `created_after`, `created_before`, `scope`. Use `list_memories` to browse without a query.

k.description: Maximum number of results to return.

as_of.description: Optional date the question is asked on, YYYY-MM-DD; today when omitted.

branch_scope.description: Which git branch's synced chunks to search: "current" (default), "all", or a branch name.

collapse_sources.description: Merge the chunks of one synced file into its best chunk. Default true; pass false to see every chunk.

created_after.description: Keep only memories written at or after this UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD) or RFC 3339 timestamp.

created_before.description: Keep only memories written before this UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD) or RFC 3339 timestamp.

dedupe_identical.description: Return a passage found word for word in several synced files once, listing the others in `also_in` (default true).

folder.description: Keep only notes under this folder of a connector.

min_relevance.description: Drop hits below this `relevance`; off by default.

object_type.description: Keep only memories of this type: a string or a list of strings.

reasoning.description: Also ask the local reasoning model for a cited answer drawn from the hits (default false).

scope.description: Restrict results to a subset of the store before ranking.

tags.description: Keep only results carrying at least one of these tags (case-sensitive, exact match).

verify.description: With `reasoning`, run two independent passes and keep only answers both agree on.

widen.description: With `reasoning`, also reason over reworded queries and linked memories.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Save a fact, preference or decision so a later conversation can recall it. Use it when the user asks you to remember something, and whenever the user states a fact, preference or decision worth keeping. Required: `text`. Optional: `tags`, `speaker`, `object_type`, `partition`, `supersedes`, `relations`, `inferred`, `similar_min_relevance`. Returns `key`. Separate from Claude's built-in memory. `partition_use` sets the session's default partition. Set `speaker: "user"` when the text is the user's own words. Correct an earlier memory with `supersedes: <key>`; `forget` on the new key reverts. `similar` lists up to 3 close existing memories; `suggested_forget` names a near-exact duplicate you may forget. `inferred: true` saves your own inference, hidden from default results until reviewed. `object_type` is a free-text label. Long text is split into pieces; `key` still works for `expand`/`forget`. Never store secrets.

tags.description: Optional tags to attach to this memory.

speaker.description: `user` for the user's own words, `assistant` for yours.

object_type.description: Optional free-text label for what kind of memory.

supersedes.description: Optional: the key of an existing memory this one corrects or replaces.

relations.description: Optional edges from this new memory to existing ones.

inferred.description: True for your own inference rather than something the user stated; hidden until reviewed.

tools.name: expand
tools.description: Fetch one memory by key: full text, tags and provenance. A split memory comes back whole whichever piece you ask for (`chunk_keys` lists the pieces; `piece_only: true` returns just the one). `truncated: true` means the text was cut at 64 KB. Unlike `recall`, this reaches pending, superseded and deleted objects. Cite `source_uri` for a "connector" source. `edges: true` adds links; `history: true` walks the `supersedes` chain.

key.description: The key to look up, as returned by `remember` or `recall`.

edges.description: Include this object's edges (both directions) in the response.

piece_only.description: When true and the key is one piece of a long memory, return only that piece.

tools.name: forget
tools.description: Forget a remembered object by key. `mode` defaults to "revert": on a chain head created with `supersedes` it tombstones the head and restores the predecessor; otherwise it tombstones the target. "chain" tombstones every version of the chain. "object" tombstones only this object. On a synced chunk `mode` is ignored: the whole source is forgotten and never re-ingested (`sync_source_id` names it).

key.description: The key to forget, as returned by `remember`.

tools.name: list_memories
tools.description: List memories by scope without a query, newest first. Use `scope: "user"` for what the user told you, or `scope: "connector:<id>"` for a synced source. Filters work as in `recall`. `count` is the total match count; pass `next_cursor` as `after_key` for the next page. Hides pending and superseded memories by default. Unknown arguments are listed in `ignored_params`.

after_key.description: Continue after this key: pass the previous page's `next_cursor`.

created_after.description: UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD) or RFC 3339 time; keep memories at or after it.

created_before.description: UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD) or RFC 3339 time; keep memories before it.

newest_first.description: `true` (default) lists newest-written first; `false` lists oldest-written first.

object_type.description: Keep only memories of this type: a string or a list of strings.

tags.description: Same as `recall`'s `tags` - keep only memories carrying at least one of these.

tools.name: partition_list
tools.description: List partitions, the namespaces that keep memories apart (for example one per client). Every store has a default "unsorted" partition. `include_archived: true` also lists archived ones.

include_archived.description: `false` (default) lists only active partitions; `true` also includes archived ones.

tools.name: partition_create
tools.description: Create a partition by name. The name may not be "current", "all", "all_active", "none", start with "id:", or match an active partition. Call `partition_use` to save into it.

display_name.description: The name for the new partition.

tools.name: partition_use
tools.description: Bind this connection to one partition (an unbound connection searches every active partition): later `remember` calls without `partition` land there, and `recall`/`list_memories` without `partition_scope` search only there. Not persisted across connections. Accepts a name or "id:<ulid>"; "all" is invalid. Returns the bound partition.

partition.description: Partition name or "id:<ulid>"; "all" and "all_active" are invalid.

annotations.title: Choose the partition for this session

tools.name: partition_rename
tools.description: Rename a partition by id. Refused for the default partition and for reserved or taken names.

id.description: The partition's id, as returned by `partition_list`/`partition_create`.

tools.name: partition_archive
tools.description: Archive a partition by id. Its memories stay reachable with `partition_scope: "id:<ulid>"`. Refused for the default partition. Idempotent.

id.description: The partition's id, as returned by `partition_list`/`partition_create`.

tools.name: partition_restore
tools.description: Restore an archived partition by id. Refused if an active partition now has its name. Idempotent.

id.description: The partition's id, as returned by `partition_list`/`partition_create`.

tools.name: diagnostics
tools.description: Report health: version, store location, `live_count`, search mode, uptime, connector sync state and degraded status. `live_breakdown` explains why `list_memories` may show fewer than `live_count`. Check `connectors[].failures` for files that did not index and `degraded` for skipped corrupt records. Not needed for normal use.

tools.name: usage
tools.description: Summarize this server's local tool-call log over the last `days`: calls per session by tool, empty recalls, saves per session and errors by code. The log holds no memory content. Not needed for normal use.

days.description: Summarize the last this-many days (1-90; default 7; the log keeps 90).

sessions.description: How many of the most recently active sessions to break down by tool (0-50).
